analysis:
The PR turns release-swift.yml into a thin caller. It routes master pushes to dev and staging lanes, tags to prod, and dispatches to the chosen environment. The signing, notarization, R2 staging and coordinator-registration chain moves into a new reusable .github/workflows/release-provider.yml, which was NOT supplied. The visible base lines 583-1280 are the logic being moved: signing identity and entitlement checks, notarization, staple and cmp, CodeDirectory hash extraction, publication artifact, per-environment secret resolution with PROD_* and legacy secrets empty unless env==prod, and publish concurrency group provider-publication-${env}. I could not verify that these controls survive the move.

Key caller facts (head release-swift.yml):
- All three lanes use `secrets: inherit`.
- Staging is gated by vars.STAGING_ENABLED and signed with the same Developer ID and team access group as dev and prod.
- Prod is selected by `github.ref_type == 'tag'` (line 160) or by a prod dispatch.
- Concurrency groups: release-dev, release-staging, and a per-run group for prod.
- Top-level permissions are contents: write and actions: read.

One low finding: a tag-ref dispatch can run the prod lane alongside the selected lane.

For the next pass: review release-provider.yml for lane isolation (secret scoping, resolve-provider-release.sh refusing prod on a non-tag trigger, the A-011 hash registry registering only to the matching coordinator, and the per-env publication concurrency). Also check that workflow_call input handling (version_override, resume_run_id) is injection-safe. The docs and changelog changes are descriptive only.

findings.detail: The `prod` job condition is `github.ref_type == 'tag' || (dispatch && environment=='prod')`, while the `dev` and `staging` jobs key off `inputs.environment`. These are independent `if`s, so a `workflow_dispatch` run against a tag ref (for example `--ref v1.2.3 -f environment=dev -f validation_only=true`) starts both the selected lane and the prod lane. The prod lane also receives `validation_only`, `version_override` and `resume_run_id`, and `secrets: inherit` gives it the production signing and release secrets. The tag-first logic in `run-name` suggests the old single workflow had similar tag precedence, but it ran one resolved lane. This PR adds explicit fan-out, so one dispatch can now sign and publish more than the operator intended. Whether prod publication then succeeds depends on `resolve-provider-release.sh`, which was not supplied. Fix: gate the prod job on `github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref_type == 'tag'` or on `inputs.environment == 'prod'` for dispatch. Also reject a dispatch whose ref type conflicts with the chosen environment.
findings.title: Tag-ref workflow_dispatch fans out to the prod lane in addition to the selected lane
